text:
devon: Heads up — since we enabled cross-region fallback for eu->us last night p99 in eu jumped from ~220ms -> ~540ms. Looks correlated with increased kernel switch + KV cache misses. Anyone seen similar?
anya: Oof. Do we have profiler traces / flamegraphs for the spikes?
devon: Uploaded a few traces to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/eu/179210-snapshots.tar.gz
       Quick summary: during fallback windows we see a lot more 'kernel_fallback' decisions in the decision log and a 3x drop in kv_hit_ratio.
sam: That matches my gut — cross-region fallback changes routing affinity so requests hit replicas without warmed KV caches and get forced onto slower kernels for compatibility.
maria: What microbatch sizes are we hitting when fallback occurs? small microbatches + cold KV = bad combo for tail.
devon: Observed microbatch median went 8 -> 20 when fallback fired (we added burst=enabled). p50=90ms, p95=210ms, p99=540ms (eu region, window 02:00-03:30UTC).
kevin: Can you paste the routing config we rolled? curious about the fallback predicate.
devon: Sure — snippet from routing policy: 
```
priority: [local, cross_region]
fallback:
  enabled: true
  when:
    - local_capacity < 0.85
    - local_queue_ms > 200
  allow_model_variant_switch: true
```

anya: Two angles: (1) kernel selection path — if we allow model_variant_switch we might be switching to variants that require different kernels (e.g., quantized vs fp16) and trigger slower kernels, (2) KV cache cold starts because routing changes locality.
sam: Agreed. Proposal: add a sticky-routing window (30s) per user/request token so cache locality isn't destroyed by transient capacity signals. Also limit cross-region fallback to only when local_latency_p95 > configured_slo instead of queue/occupancy.
maria: Also test microbatch tuning — lowering target_microbatch from 32 -> 12 for cross-region flows might reduce serialization latency while keeping throughput reasonable. We should A/B it.
devon: infra-bot: deploy rollback check ran — no automatic rollback triggered. :information_source:
infra-bot: deploy 1792.210 -> routing/fallback-v2 applied to eu at 01:58 UTC by @devon
kevin: For the A/B we must capture metrics: kv_hit_ratio, tail_latency_by_route (p50/p95/p99), kernel_switch_count, effective_batched_tokens. Without those we won't know if it's kernel or cache.
anya: I drafted an experiment config: 
```
experiment:
  groups:
    control: routing/fallback-v2 (sticky disabled)
    variant: routing/fallback-v2-sticky
  sample: 10% eu traffic
  metrics: [kv_hit_ratio, p99_latency, kernel_switch_count]
  duration: 30m
```

sam: Also run a kernel-forcing micro-experiment: force fused-attn-v2 for both groups for 15m to see delta. If p99 drops despite low kv_hit_ratio then kernel is likely root cause.
maria: Action items: (1) devon -> start 10% A/B sticky vs control for 30m, collect metrics; (2) sam -> prepare kernel-forced run; (3) anya -> post profiler traces linking kernel switch stack samples; (4) kevin -> add dashboard cards for tail_latency_by_route and kv_hit_ratio with 1m resolution.
devon: I'll kick off the A/B in 10m and drop updates here. Also adding temp alert: if eu.p99 > 450ms revert fallback.
kevin: If we see kernel_switch_count spike, we should consider fallback kernel compatibility matrix: maybe disallow model_variant_switch during cross-region fallback until kv warmed.
anya: Good point — we can also try optimistic warmup: prefetch KV for the top N prefixes when routing chooses a new replica. Small warmup could eliminate most cold misses.
sam: Sounds good. Keep it tight — these are user-facing SLOs. :rocket: 
devon: Update 30m later: kicked off experiment at 03:05 UTC — initial 10m shows kv_hit_ratio in variant + sticky = 0.78 vs control 0.42, p99 variant = 260ms vs control = 520ms. Will continue run and post final numbers.
maria: Nice! If that holds we have a clear mitigation path: sticky routing + small warmup + guard on kernel switching when fallback triggers.
kevin: Perfect — schedule follow-up postmortem if numbers regress after scaling.
anya: Thanks all — I'll attach the flamegraphs to the experiment ticket when the run completes. :thumbsup:
